use: The background behind something, often private: jijou ga aru (there are reasons I'd rather not explain).

example.romaji: ironna jijou ga atte, ikenaku natta
example.ja: いろんな事情があって、行けなくなった
example.english: Some things came up, so now I can't go.

examplePolite.romaji: iroiro na jijou ga atte, ikenaku narimashita
examplePolite.ja: いろいろな事情があって、行けなくなりました
examplePolite.english: Due to various circumstances, I'm no longer able to go.

notes: A polite, vague way to avoid explaining. Joukyou is the situation as it stands now.

use: Checks or insists that someone means it: honki? (are you serious?), honki da yo (I mean it).

example.romaji: honki de kare to kekkon suru tsumori?
example.ja: 本気で彼と結婚するつもり?
example.english: Are you seriously going to marry him?

examplePolite.romaji: honki de kare to kekkon suru tsumori desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 本気で彼と結婚するつもりですか?
examplePolite.english: Are you seriously planning to marry him?

notes: Honki de = seriously, with real effort. Honki ni suru = take a joke at face value.

use: How someone acts toward others, usually judged: taido ga warui (rude), sono taido nani? (what's with that attitude?).

example.romaji: kare, saikin taido ga tsumetai
example.ja: 彼、最近態度が冷たい
example.english: He's been acting cold lately.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa saikin taido ga tsumetai desu
examplePolite.ja: 彼は最近態度が冷たいです
examplePolite.english: He's been acting cold toward me lately.

notes: Taido is outward behavior; the feeling inside is kimochi. Taido ga dekai = acting like you own the place.

use: Usually yuuki o dasu (work up the courage) or yuuki ga nai (not have the nerve).

example.romaji: yuuki dashite kokuhaku shita
example.ja: 勇気出して告白した
example.english: I worked up the courage and told them how I felt.

examplePolite.romaji: yuuki o dashite kokuhaku shimashita
examplePolite.ja: 勇気を出して告白しました
examplePolite.english: I worked up the courage and told them how I felt.

notes: Yuuki o morau = be encouraged by someone or something.

use: Almost always zenryoku de (with all your might) or zenryoku o tsukusu (give it your all).

example.romaji: saigo made zenryoku de ganbaru yo
example.ja: 最後まで全力で頑張るよ
example.english: I'll give it everything right to the end.

examplePolite.romaji: saigo made zenryoku de ganbarimasu
examplePolite.ja: 最後まで全力で頑張ります
examplePolite.english: I'll give it everything right to the end.

notes: Also used jokingly: zenryoku de kotowaru (refuse flat out).

use: Self-respect that gets hurt or gets in the way: puraido ga takai (too proud to back down).

example.romaji: kare wa puraido ga takai kara ayamaranai yo
example.ja: 彼はプライドが高いから謝らないよ
example.english: He's too proud to apologize.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa puraido ga takai node ayamaranai to omoimasu
examplePolite.ja: 彼はプライドが高いので謝らないと思います
examplePolite.english: I think he's too proud to apologize.

notes: Puraido ga kizutsuku = your pride gets hurt. Being proud of something good is hokori.

use: A natural gift: ~ no sainou ga aru (have a talent for ~).

example.romaji: e no sainou aru yo ne
example.ja: 絵の才能あるよね
example.english: You've really got a talent for drawing.

examplePolite.romaji: e no sainou ga arimasu ne
examplePolite.ja: 絵の才能がありますね
examplePolite.english: You have a real talent for drawing.

notes: Sainou is inborn; jitsuryoku is proven skill; nouryoku is ability in general.

use: Ability in general, often for work or study; in dramas also superpowers.

example.romaji: kare wa nouryoku wa takai kedo, yaru ki ga nai
example.ja: 彼は能力は高いけど、やる気がない
example.english: He's very capable, but he's got no drive.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa nouryoku wa takai desu ga, yaru ki ga arimasen
examplePolite.ja: 彼は能力は高いですが、やる気がありません
examplePolite.english: He's very capable, but he has no drive.

notes: Chounouryoku = supernatural powers. Day to day, 'can do' is just dekiru.

use: The skill you actually show, in contests or at work; often set against luck.

example.romaji: un ja nakute jitsuryoku da yo
example.ja: 運じゃなくて実力だよ
example.english: That wasn't luck, that was skill.

examplePolite.romaji: un de wa naku jitsuryoku desu yo
examplePolite.ja: 運ではなく実力ですよ
examplePolite.english: That wasn't luck, that was real skill.

notes: Jitsuryoku o dasu = perform at your true level.

use: Emotional hurt or disappointment: shokku! (I'm gutted), shokku o ukeru (be hit hard).

example.romaji: sore kiite, maji de shokku datta
example.ja: それ聞いて、マジでショックだった
example.english: Hearing that really hurt.

examplePolite.romaji: sore o kiite, hontou ni shokku deshita
examplePolite.ja: それを聞いて、本当にショックでした
examplePolite.english: I was really upset to hear that.

notes: Mostly 'hurt and let down', not surprise; for surprise say bikkuri.

use: Used loosely for any awful situation.

example.romaji: manin densha, maiasa jigoku da yo
example.ja: 満員電車、毎朝地獄だよ
example.english: The packed train is hell every morning.

examplePolite.romaji: manin densha wa maiasa jigoku desu
examplePolite.ja: 満員電車は毎朝地獄です
examplePolite.english: The packed train is hell every morning.

notes: Opposite: tengoku (heaven).

english: go through (a feeling); have a (hard, lonely...) time
use: Always after a feeling word: tsurai omoi o suru (have a hard time), hazukashii omoi o suru (be embarrassed).

example.romaji: kodomo no koro, sabishii omoi o shita
example.ja: 子供の頃、寂しい思いをした
example.english: I was lonely a lot as a kid.

examplePolite.romaji: kodomo no koro, sabishii omoi o shimashita
examplePolite.ja: 子供の頃、寂しい思いをしました
examplePolite.english: I was often lonely as a child.

notes: Omoi o saseru = put someone through it: tsurai omoi sasete gomen (sorry for putting you through so much).

use: Real life as opposed to dreams, plans or fiction.

example.romaji: genjitsu wa sonna ni amakunai yo
example.ja: 現実はそんなに甘くないよ
example.english: Real life isn't that easy.

examplePolite.romaji: genjitsu wa sonna ni amaku arimasen yo
examplePolite.ja: 現実はそんなに甘くありませんよ
examplePolite.english: Real life isn't that easy.

notes: Genjitsu o miro = face reality. Genjitsuteki = realistic.

use: In quick prayers and exclamations, and as praise for someone who saved the day.

example.romaji: kamisama, onegai! goukaku sasete!
example.ja: 神様、お願い!合格させて!
example.english: Please, God, let me pass!

examplePolite.romaji: kamisama, dou ka goukaku dekimasu you ni
examplePolite.ja: 神様、どうか合格できますように
examplePolite.english: Please, God, let me pass.

notes: Slang: kami alone means 'amazing' (kami da! = that's awesome).

use: Your ideal of something: risou no taipu (ideal type), risou ga takai (have high standards).

example.romaji: risou no kareshi tte donna hito?
example.ja: 理想の彼氏ってどんな人?
example.english: What's your ideal boyfriend like?

examplePolite.romaji: risou no kareshi wa donna hito desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 理想の彼氏はどんな人ですか?
examplePolite.english: What would your ideal boyfriend be like?

notes: Often paired with genjitsu: risou to genjitsu (the ideal vs reality). Risouteki = ideal (as an adjective).

use: Something that by rights shouldn't have happened, often said with relief or exaggeration.

example.romaji: shiken ni ukatta no wa kiseki da yo
example.ja: 試験に受かったのは奇跡だよ
example.english: Me passing that exam was a miracle.

examplePolite.romaji: shiken ni ukatta no wa kiseki desu
examplePolite.ja: 試験に受かったのは奇跡です
examplePolite.english: Passing that exam was a miracle.

notes: Kiseki ga okiru = a miracle happens. Kisekiteki ni = miraculously.

use: Goes before a noun for a first experience: hatsu deeto (first date), hatsu taiken (first time trying something).

example.romaji: kyou ga kanojo to no hatsu deeto da yo
example.ja: 今日が彼女との初デートだよ
example.english: Today's my first date with her.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou ga kanojo to no hatsu deeto desu
examplePolite.ja: 今日が彼女との初デートです
examplePolite.english: Today is my first date with her.

notes: 'For the first time' is hajimete. The same kanji is read sho in shonichi (opening day).

use: Short for a ceremony both people know about, usually the wedding: shiki wa itsu? (when's the wedding?).

example.romaji: shiki wa rainen no haru ni suru
example.ja: 式は来年の春にする
example.english: We're having the wedding next spring.

examplePolite.romaji: shiki wa rainen no haru ni shimasu
examplePolite.ja: 式は来年の春にします
examplePolite.english: We're holding the wedding next spring.

notes: Full forms: kekkonshiki (wedding), sotsugyoushiki (graduation). In compounds it can also mean 'style' or 'formula'.

english: commemoration; keepsake; to mark the occasion
use: Mostly kinen ni (as a keepsake, to mark the day) and in compounds.

example.romaji: kinen ni issho ni shashin torou yo
example.ja: 記念に一緒に写真撮ろうよ
example.english: Let's take a photo together to remember this.

examplePolite.romaji: kinen ni issho ni shashin o torimashou
examplePolite.ja: 記念に一緒に写真を撮りましょう
examplePolite.english: Let's take a photo together to mark the occasion.

notes: Kinenbi = anniversary. Kinen shashin = a photo to mark the day.

use: After a verb or noun to mean 'in case of' or 'if': okureru baai wa (if you'll be late).

example.romaji: okureru baai wa renraku shite ne
example.ja: 遅れる場合は連絡してね
example.english: If you're going to be late, let me know.

examplePolite.romaji: okureru baai wa renraku shite kudasai
examplePolite.ja: 遅れる場合は連絡してください
examplePolite.english: If you're going to be late, please let us know.

notes: Sonna koto itteru baai ja nai = this is no time to be saying that.
